modules.title: Insurance & Risk Protection for Civil Servants
modules.summary: One hospital stay can wipe out years of savings. Understand NHIMA, funeral cover, and what a claim actually requires, so a disaster does not become a debt trap.

lessons.title: Why insurance is the most underused tool by civil servants
lessons.content:
# Why insurance is the most underused tool by civil servants

Insurance is the one product civil servants buy only when they wish they had. The gap is not income - it is that nobody has explained what cover costs, what it pays, and what a claim requires.

## Why so few of us have cover

Zambia's insurance penetration is **1.20% of GDP** (K6,032 million gross written premium in 2022) against a global average of about **7%**. The Bank of Zambia's National Financial Inclusion Strategy II names the barriers: *"limited financial and digital literacy"* and *"cultural factors inhibiting the uptake of ... life insurance products and funeral policy."* Claims paid rose from **K1,887.8 million in Q3 2024 to K2,512.8 million by end-Q3 2025**.

## NHIMA: what you already have, and what it really does

NHIMA is compulsory health cover. Your employer deducts **1% of your basic salary** and adds a further **1%**, remitted monthly within 10 days of the month end. The base is **basic salary** - allowances sit outside it - and there is **no earnings ceiling**. Informal households pay about **K50 per household per month** for up to seven members.

**The waiting period is 4 months, not six.** A fully paid member can only access services 4 months after registration. Members aged 65 and above have no waiting period at all.

**Dental and vision are covered** - the belief that they are excluded is wrong. NHIMA's benefit package covers out-patient and in-patient care, ICU and HDU; diagnostics (X-ray, CT, MRI, ultrasound, mammogram); major and minor surgery; maternity, neonatal and paediatric care; pharmaceuticals and blood products; physiotherapy; mental health; oncology; medical appliances and prostheses; **dental and oral health** (fillings, gum treatment, extractions, braces, dentures, root canal); and **vision care and spectacles** - spectacles **once every three years**, plus cataract, glaucoma and trauma care.

**Who does not pay but must still register:** persons 65 and above; persons declared poor and vulnerable by the social welfare ministry; and persons who are mentally or physically disabled and unable to work.

**Your dependants.** NHIMA's FAQ says **6 beneficiaries** (spouse plus 5 dependants under 18); the July 2024 Ministerial Statement to Parliament says "one plus six" - a principal plus up to six family members, covering seven. The sources conflict, so **confirm with NHIMA on 8000 before registering dependants.** A dependant who turns 18 registers as a principal and contributes separately. If the principal dies, registered family members keep benefits for **4 months**.

## Funeral cover: the one product worth your money

A funeral policy pays a cash lump sum when an insured person dies. It needs **no medical exam**, and it pays out exactly when a family is least able to pay.

**The waiting period is the killer.** Common waiting periods are **3 to 6 months**: Zanaco Flexi Farewell charges 6 months for death from natural causes; FSG and ideal group plans charge 3 months, waived for accidental death, but **24 months for suicide**. If the insured dies inside the waiting period, **nothing is paid**. "Do not die in the first six months" is the most common reason a funeral policy pays nothing.

## What a claim actually requires

| Document | Note |
|---|---|
| Claim form | Signed by the claimant; if they cannot sign, a **fingerprint certified by a Commissioner of Oaths at a police station** |
| Death certificate | Or a burial order / medical certificate of cause of death |
| Certified NRC of the deceased | National ID |
| Certified birth certificate | For a child |
| Certified ID of the claimant | |
| Proof of relationship | Marriage or birth certificate |
| Police report | **Only where the death was accidental** |
| Policy document | |

**Submit the claim within 6 months of the date of death and all documentation within 12 months** - the insurer may reject a late claim. If no beneficiary was nominated, the spouse inherits; failing that the closest qualifying relative who is insured; failing that the estate.

## If the insurer refuses

Complain to the insurer first. If it is not resolved, escalate to the **Pensions and Insurance Authority (PIA)**: it acknowledges complaints within 3 days and investigates within 10 business days. PIA now issues **Key Fact Statements** for funeral and life policies. Ask any agent: *"Can I have the Key Fact Statement in writing before I sign?"*

> **What to do this week**
> 1. Check your NHIMA record: is your dependant list complete, and has anyone turned 18?
> 2. Ask an insurer for the Key Fact Statement and the waiting period in writing, before you sign.
> 3. Optional: keep the claim document list above in one folder at home and tell your family where it is.
>
> **Where to check**
> NHIMA on 8000 for registration, dependants and the 4-month waiting period; the Pensions and Insurance Authority (pia.org.zm) for licensed insurers and complaints.

modules.title: Why Your Cooperative is Your Best Investment
modules.summary: For most Zambian civil servants, the cooperative is the best financial deal they will ever see. Here is the honest math, and what it asks of you.

lessons.title: The 5% return that beats the bank
lessons.content:
# The 5% return that beats the bank

The title of this lesson needs one honest correction before anything else. **The 5% is a rate you borrow at, not a rate you earn.** The cooperative does not pay you 5% on your money, and it guarantees you nothing. What it gives you is a savings system you cannot quietly spend, and credit at a rate no commercial lender in Zambia would offer.

## What your K100 a month actually does

Since the General Meeting of 2026-10-12, every Kwacha you contribute is split by the Constitution (Art. 4.1) into four live buckets:

| Bucket | Share |
|---|---|
| Land and Capital Reserve | **60%** |
| Business Seed Fund | **20%** |
| Soft Loans | **15%** |
| Admin and Audit | **5%** |

**The funeral and medical welfare buckets were closed at that same meeting.** The cooperative no longer pays a funeral or medical benefit. If you need one, you now need a funeral policy from an insurer - see the insurance lesson in this hub.

## The honest comparison

| | Rate | Date |
|---|---|---|
| Average commercial bank lending rate | **27.5%** | June 2026 |
| Microfinance institutions | 25% to 50% per annum; some quote 4% to 10% per month | UN-REDD and CAHF |
| Savings groups ("chilimba") | 5% to 20% per month | UN-REDD, 2026 |
| Money-lenders legal cap | 48% per year, and compound interest is illegal | Money-Lenders Act (Cap 398) |
| **BISWIC soft loan** | **5% per annum** | Constitution Art. 5.5 |
| 6-month bank deposit rate | 7.4% | June 2026 |
| **Headline inflation** | **6.1%** | September 2026 |

Read the last three rows carefully. **A 6-month bank deposit at 7.4% beats inflation of 6.1% by about 1.3 percentage points - better than the cooperative's earning rate.** The Bank of Zambia only reported that the real savings rate turned positive in February 2026, after a long run of negative real returns.

So the cooperative is **not** a clever financial trick. It is two things a bank will not give you:

1. **Forced, monthly saving you cannot quietly spend.** Only 11.1% of Zambians say savings is their main emergency money; 34.9% say family or friends. 65.8% save through mobile money - the wallet you shop from.
2. **Cheap credit, on your own terms.** Art. 5.5: maximum **K3,000** principal at any one time, **6-month** maximum term, **5% per annum**, eligibility after **6 months'** membership, two missed payments means default, and two of the three sub-committee members must approve.

## What you get back is not a guaranteed return

What a member receives is set by law and by the members themselves, not by a rate card:

- A **dividend** on share capital is **capped at 6% per annum**.
- **No dividend or bonus may be declared or paid before the financial statements are certified by a qualified auditor.** A bonus announced with no auditor's report is a warning, not good news.
- Surplus must be distributed within **12 months** of the financial year end.
- In a working society the **patronage bonus**, paid on the business you brought in, is usually larger than the dividend.

And your money is **not a deposit**. Withdrawal is governed by the by-laws, not by demand at the counter.

## What it asks of you

Contribute every month without exception. Attend the AGM: the agenda is fixed by law, and you may **require an audited statement** of receipts, expenditure, assets and liabilities within **six months** of the financial year end, and inspect the latest balance sheet and audit report. One member has one vote and **no proxies** - your shares buy no extra votes. One-third of the members can demand an inquiry by the **Registrar of Co-operative Societies**, and where the committee fails to call the AGM, the Registrar calls it.

Do not borrow to build savings. Borrowing from the soft loan to seed an emergency fund makes you a defaulter and weakens the bucket every other member depends on.

> **What to do this week**
> 1. Check that your contribution for last month is actually recorded - the discipline only works if the money is there.
> 2. Write down the date of the last AGM and ask the secretary for the audited statement.
> 3. Optional: set a target fund for one specific goal - goal cost divided by paydays remaining - and transfer it on payday.
>
> **Where to check**
> The Registrar of Co-operative Societies (Ministry of SMEs) for the society's registration, returns and any inquiry; the Bank of Zambia for the rate and inflation figures above.

modules.title: Avoiding Scams: Sakawa, Kachalo & Pyramid Schemes in Zambia
modules.summary: Zambia is fertile ground for every kind of fraud. Here are the scams operating now, how to spot each in 60 seconds, and the exact numbers to report them to.

lessons.title: The 10 most common scams in Zambia (and how to spot them)
lessons.content:
# The 10 most common scams in Zambia (and how to spot them)

First, the word. **"Sakawa" is a Hausa word meaning "putting inside", borrowed from the West African online-fraud ecosystem and now used loosely in Zambia for Ponzi and pyramid schemes.** It is not advance-fee fraud, which is a **different crime**. Zambia's law has its own name for it: under **section 157 of the Banking and Financial Services Act**, conducting or participating in a **"money circulation scheme"** is an offence, and that is the name you need when you report.

Bank of Zambia's definition: *"an unsustainable investment operation that pays returns to its investors from their own money or the money paid by subsequent investors, rather than from profit earned by the individual or organization running the operation."*

## The scale of it

| Figure | Value |
|---|---|
| Online scam cases recorded, 2023 to mid-2024 | **1,124** |
| Value lost | **over K38,948,000** |
| Value recovered | **K12,407,990** (about 32%) |
| Cases in court / convictions secured | 560 / **117** |
| Average per case | about **K34,700** - one to two months of net salary |
| SIM cards deactivated for mobile money fraud, Jan to Jun 2026 | **43,500**, securing **K19.8 million** (90,000 blocked in 2025) |
| Saved by the reporting code alone, first half of 2025 | **K21 million** |

Mobile money carried **4,948,992,296 transactions worth K891.7 billion in 2025 - 97.4% of all payments by number** - and drove financial inclusion to **76.2%**. Fraud here is a quantified hit on savings, not a nuisance.

## The 10 scams

| # | Scam | The tell, in 60 seconds |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Money circulation scheme** ("sakawa") | It asks you to **recruit others**. The SEC's test: *"The moment they ask you to recruit others, just know there is a problem."* |
| 2 | **Fake job or recruitment fee** | No employer asks for a registration, exam or "visa" fee. The ACC: no money was required for a government job. |
| 3 | **Overseas job and trafficking** | Verify the recruiter before you travel or hand over a passport. On arrival it is taken. |
| 4 | **Advance-fee fraud** | Each fee "releases" the next one. The fee never ends. |
| 5 | **Romance scam** | A long online relationship ending in a request for money, and the person **refuses a live video call**. |
| 6 | **"Guaranteed" investment or crypto** | Easy withdrawals at first, then blocked. Check SEC's "Find a Licensee" register before paying. |
| 7 | **Deepfake of an official** | A video of the Bank of Zambia Governor endorsing a platform. The Bank *"neither operates, endorses, nor promotes"* such platforms. |
| 8 | **Mobile money fraud** | "Your account has been compromised", a merchant refund, a fake reversal, or a request to approve a payment. |
| 9 | **SIM swap or identity theft** | Your phone suddenly loses signal, then money moves out of your wallet. ZICTA has capped SIM registrations per person at **10**. |
| 10 | **Fake online store, or a government SMS** | Comments turned off, prices too good, or an SMS asking you to "verify" bank details - the Government never requests bank details by SMS or WhatsApp. |

**Two habits prevent most of it.** Never share your PIN - **even with family** - and always read the **recipient's name** on your screen before you authorise a transfer.

## Where to report: save these now

| Channel | Use it for |
|---|---|
| **\*707#** | Report a scammer's number or a stolen phone, on all networks. ZICTA warns that false reporting may get **your own SIM deactivated**. |
| **\*101#** | Check how many numbers are registered against your National Registration Card |
| **7070** | ZICTA call centre |
| **5678** | CCPC complaints, toll free. Contact the trader first and bring proof of transaction; the CCPC acknowledges within 24 to 48 hours and resolves every complaint within **90 days** |
| **Police** | Criminal fraud, identity theft and trafficking - nearest station |
| **SEC Zambia** (seczambia.org.zm) | Public alerts and "Find a Licensee" - for anything presented as an investment |
| **Bank of Zambia** (boz.zm) | Deposit-taking, money circulation schemes, impersonation of the Bank or the Governor |
| **ACC** | Recruitment scams involving public officials |

**If you have already been scammed:** stop sending money; screenshot the chats, the transaction and the number; report fast with that evidence; tell your family. Shame keeps people inside scams.

> **What to do this week**
> 1. Save the three short codes - \*707#, \*101# and 5678 - in your phone contacts now, before you need them.
> 2. Run \*101# and check how many numbers are registered against your National Registration Card.
> 3. Optional: agree with one relative who would receive money for you first, and how much.
>
> **Where to check**
> The Consumer Competition Commission on 5678 for trader disputes; the Securities and Exchange Commission of Zambia (seczambia.org.zm) before you put money into anything presented as an investment.
